status: Proposed developer reference labels; pharmacist review pending.

labels.label: consistent
labels.rationale: The two written regimens match.

labels.label: consistent
labels.rationale: Daily and once daily describe the same frequency here.

labels.label: change
labels.rationale: The later record explicitly describes a change to 10 mg.

labels.label: change
labels.rationale: The later record explicitly changes the frequency.

labels.label: stopped
labels.rationale: The later record explicitly stops the target medicine.

labels.label: stopped
labels.rationale: The stop instruction names Alphamed; the other medicine is separate.

labels.label: missing
labels.rationale: Alphamed is omitted from the later record without a stop instruction.

labels.label: missing
labels.rationale: A different medicine is listed later; no substitution or stop is documented.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: The earlier unexplained 5-to-10 mg discrepancy remains unresolved; a later matching change instruction does not explain it.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: The explicit final change does not explain the earlier undocumented increase.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: Both dose transitions lack an explicit explanation; returning to the earlier dose does not erase the discrepancy.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: Different doses share a document date, so their order is unknown.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: The two latest records disagree on the same date. A change word does not establish their order.

labels.label: consistent
labels.rationale: Same-date records agree on the written instruction; no ordering assumption is needed.

labels.label: change
labels.rationale: An explicit start follows an explicit stop; this is a documented transition, not proof of treatment suitability.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: A continue instruction follows a stop without an explicit restart explanation.

labels.label: stopped
labels.rationale: Both records explicitly stop the medicine. No restart is documented.

labels.label: unresolved
labels.rationale: A conditional hold has no known endpoint here and cannot be reduced to a permanent stop or a single regimen.

labels.label: unresolved
labels.rationale: The later frequency is missing, preventing a supported comparison of the full instruction.

labels.label: unresolved
labels.rationale: A multi-stage taper with relative timing cannot be reduced to one dated instruction from these records.

labels.label: unresolved
labels.rationale: An invalid document date prevents a supported ordering.

labels.label: unresolved
labels.rationale: The second document has no date, so its temporal relation is unknown.

labels.label: change
labels.rationale: The later-dated record explicitly changes the dose; input order is irrelevant.

labels.label: consistent
labels.rationale: One gram equals 1,000 milligrams. The amount, route, and frequency agree despite different unit notation.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: The route changes without an explicit explanation. This task does not judge whether either route is appropriate.

labels.label: conflict
labels.rationale: The decimal changes the amount tenfold with no documented explanation.

labels.label: missing
labels.rationale: The target is missing in the later record; this does not establish discontinuation.

labels.label: stopped
labels.rationale: The latest available target-specific instruction is an explicit stop; the later unrelated record does not document a restart.

labels.label: new
labels.rationale: Alphamed is first documented in the supplied records. This is not evidence of the actual treatment start date.

labels.label: change
labels.rationale: The later wording explicitly increases the amount; this meaning is clear to a human reviewer.

labels.label: stopped
labels.rationale: The later wording explicitly discontinues the medicine.

labels.label: consistent
labels.rationale: The negated stop is followed by the same complete continue instruction. A stop must not be inferred from the negated word.
